visual_argument: A Permian tank battery's own float gauge board, its target set at the computed crude share of the company's output, so a reader sees that a little under half of every barrel of oil equivalent was crude without reading the number.
build_risk: The share is a level on a thin board on a large tank, so the board, its scale and its target have to read at 432 px against dark tank paint, over a containment wall, with the tank in the pool and the type kept off the tank tops. The first evidence frame (one hour of the fastest well as a pipe column, then as a notched rule) failed the art review twice: a hairline at true scale, then a circular encoding of hours in a day. It was dropped for this frame and for the sucker rod ratio on frame 5.
distinct_from_recent: No. 67 was a floodlit weigh station with a white tractor and steel reliefs; this is lastLight on a caliche pad with a kit pump jack and a vertical column. No. 66 was San Antonio streets and a phone camera with primitive screens; nothing here is a screen. No. 65 was a foundry robot arm in primitives with dogbone tiles; the only machine here is the kit's true linkage pump jack and the one relief is two cast iron masses with no plate edge.
